newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian finance minister says bourse needs reform.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian finance minister says bourse needs reform.

text.p: Finance minister Anthony Ani on Thursday said the stock exchange and its regulatory body would have to be reformed if Nigeria was to attract foreign investment.

"The stock exchange must adopt modern methods, techniques and technology if it is to compete with other stock exchanges in the world," Ani said as he received a confidential report into Nigeria's capital markets.
The military government set up a committee in April to make suggestions on how the market could be made more dynamic and encourage the foreign investment that Nigeria badly wants.

"The pattern of governance and the management of the Stock Exchange has been poor and unimaginitive and as a result not developed the capital market...and it is not likely to do so in the forseeable future unless there are changes," he added.
Ani also criticised the regulatory Securities and Exchange Commission for being unnaccountable, and said it would have to change.

Attempts to attract foreign portfolio investors since the military government said it internationalised the exchange in 1995 have been frustrated by the absence of the necessary enabling laws and an efficient clearing and settlement system.
Last month the exchange said it would cut transaction fees as part of deregulation efforts.

But on Wednesday trade was flattened by a stockbrokers protest against the imposition of a new half percent fee. The protest ended on Thursday after agreement that the new charge would not be imposed before 1997.
The capitalisation of the stock exchange, founded in 1961, now stands at over 250 billion naira ($3.1 billion).
